steps.title: Error 1062
steps.body: 'Duplicate entry for key PRIMARY' on a replica usually means someone wrote directly to the replica, or the replica was seeded inconsistently.

steps.title: Protect replicas
steps.body: `super_read_only = ON` on replicas.

steps.title: Don't
steps.body: Blindly skipping transactions hides drift — verify with pt-table-checksum.

ticket.description: Alert: db-my02 Replica_SQL_Running=No. Reports dashboard shows yesterday's data.

investigate.label: SHOW REPLICA STATUS\G
investigate.reveal: Last_SQL_Errno: 1062 Duplicate entry '88123' for key 'coupons.PRIMARY' on query INSERT INTO coupons …

investigate.label: Check super_read_only on replica
investigate.reveal: super_read_only = OFF; read_only = OFF.

investigate.label: General log / audit on replica
investigate.reveal: A support engineer inserted coupon 88123 directly on db-my02 yesterday to 'test'.

investigate.label: Network between source and replica
investigate.reveal: Fine, IO thread is running.

options: A manual write on the writable replica created a conflicting row
diagnosis.why: The replica wasn't read-only; a direct insert conflicted with the replicated insert.

resolution: Compare the conflicting row on source and replica
Delete the test row on the replica (or inject an empty transaction for that GTID if rows match)
START REPLICA and confirm both threads Yes and lag falling
Set super_read_only = ON on all replicas (persist in config)
Run pt-table-checksum to confirm no other drift

closure.model: Root cause: replica db-my02 was writable; a manual INSERT of coupon 88123 conflicted with the replicated row (error 1062). Fix: removed the test row, restarted replication, enabled super_read_only. Verified: IO/SQL threads Yes, lag 0 after 12 min, pt-table-checksum clean.

lessons.title: Lab: Ticket — InnoDB deadlocks and lock waits

scenes.text: Inventory updates fail with 'Deadlock found when trying to get lock'.
Read SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS.

steps.title: InnoDB locking
steps.body: Row locks on index records, gap/next-key locks under REPEATABLE READ (default). Error 1205 = lock wait timeout (`innodb_lock_wait_timeout`, default 50 s); 1213 = deadlock (victim rolled back). `performance_schema.data_locks` and `sys.innodb_lock_waits` show waits.

steps.title: Fixes
steps.body: Consistent row order, smaller transactions, proper indexes (unindexed WHERE locks many rows), retry on 1213.

steps.title: Mistake
steps.body: Raising innodb_lock_wait_timeout instead of fixing long transactions.

ticket.description: Since the bulk-import job started at 10:00, pickers' stock updates sometimes fail with 'Deadlock found when trying to get lock; try restarting transaction'.

investigate.label: SHOW ENGINE INNODB STATUS — LATEST DETECTED DEADLOCK
investigate.reveal: TX1 (import): UPDATE stock SET qty=… WHERE warehouse_id=3 (no index on warehouse_id) holds many record locks; TX2 (picker): UPDATE stock … WHERE sku='A17' waits; TX1 then waits for TX2's lock.

investigate.label: Check indexes on stock
investigate.reveal: PRIMARY(sku), no index on warehouse_id.

investigate.label: Import job transaction size
investigate.reveal: Commits once at the end of 400k rows.

investigate.label: Disk latency
investigate.reveal: 2 ms — normal.

options: Huge import transaction locking many rows via an unindexed WHERE
diagnosis.why: Without an index on warehouse_id the UPDATE scans and locks many rows for a long time, colliding with pickers.

resolution: Add index on stock(warehouse_id, sku) online (ALGORITHM=INPLACE, LOCK=NONE)
Change the import to commit in batches of 1,000 rows
Add retry-on-1213 logic in both apps
Re-run import in a quiet window and watch sys.innodb_lock_waits
Close with deadlock count trend

closure.model: Root cause: the 10:00 bulk import ran one 400k-row transaction with UPDATE … WHERE warehouse_id=3 on an unindexed column, locking most of the table and deadlocking with picker updates. Fix: added index (warehouse_id, sku) online, batched commits of 1,000, retry on 1213. Verified: next import produced 0 deadlocks; lock waits < 50 ms.

options: InnoDB locks the rows it scans

lessons.title: Lab: Recovery models and backup types

steps.title: Recovery models
steps.body:
- **SIMPLE**: log truncates at checkpoint; no PITR
- **FULL**: needs log backups; PITR possible
- **BULK_LOGGED**: minimal logging for bulk ops
Backups: FULL, DIFFERENTIAL (since last full), LOG (since last log backup). `COPY_ONLY` doesn't break the chain.

steps.title: AG basics

steps.title: Rolling patch

steps.title: Mistake

lessons.title: Lab: Ticket — blocking chain at month-end

scenes.text: Finance users' screens hang during the month-end close.
Find the head blocker with DMVs.

steps.title: DMVs
steps.body: `sys.dm_exec_requests` (blocking_session_id, wait_type), `sys.dm_exec_sessions`, `sys.dm_tran_locks`, `sp_WhoIsActive` (community proc). Head blocker = blocking others but not blocked itself.

steps.title: Isolation
steps.body: READ COMMITTED SNAPSHOT (RCSI) lets readers avoid blocking on writers' locks using row versions in tempdb.

steps.title: Don't
steps.body: Don't sprinkle NOLOCK — it reads dirty, duplicated or missing rows.

ticket.description: Multiple finance users say the ERP 'freezes' when posting journals since ~16:05. Nothing errors, it just spins.

investigate.label: Query sys.dm_exec_requests for blocking_session_id
investigate.reveal: 34 requests waiting LCK_M_S / LCK_M_X; all chains lead to session 87.

investigate.label: Inspect session 87
investigate.reveal: Status sleeping, open_transaction_count = 1, last batch 16:03 from SSMS by user r.verma: BEGIN TRAN; UPDATE GL_Periods SET status='CLOSING' …; (no COMMIT).

investigate.label: CPU and memory
investigate.reveal: CPU 12%, PLE healthy.

investigate.label: Network to app servers
investigate.reveal: Normal latency.

options: An uncommitted manual transaction in SSMS holding locks on GL_Periods
diagnosis.why: A sleeping session with an open transaction is the head blocker.

resolution: Contact r.verma to COMMIT or ROLLBACK if intended
If unreachable and approved, KILL 87 (rolls back)
Confirm blocked requests drain and users can post
Educate: no open transactions in SSMS on production; use change process
Consider enabling RCSI after testing to reduce reader blocking

closure.model: Root cause: session 87 (SSMS, r.verma) ran BEGIN TRAN + UPDATE GL_Periods at 16:03 without COMMIT, holding X locks; ERP posting sessions queued behind it. Fix: with approval, KILL 87 (rollback 2 s). Verified: blocked requests drained by 16:41; users posting normally. Follow-up: SSMS production guidelines, RCSI evaluation.

options: Blocks others but isn't blocked itself

quiz.q: Why avoid NOLOCK as a fix?

options: Reading row versions instead of waiting on writers

investigate.reveal: Process A: UPDATE dbo.Orders … then UPDATE dbo.Loyalty …; Process B (nightly-ish trigger job running every minute): UPDATE dbo.Loyalty … then UPDATE dbo.Orders …; both KEY locks.

investigate.label: Indexes on Loyalty(customer_id)
investigate.reveal: Present.

investigate.label: Trigger code
investigate.reveal: trg_Loyalty_sync updates Loyalty then Orders in a different order from the order service.

investigate.label: tempdb usage
investigate.reveal: Normal.

options: Order service and loyalty sync touch Orders and Loyalty in opposite order
diagnosis.why: Classic lock-ordering deadlock between two code paths.

resolution: Change the sync job to update Orders before Loyalty (same order as the service)
Keep both transactions short
Add retry with backoff on 1205 in the order service
Monitor deadlocks via system_health / alerts for a week
Close with trend evidence

closure.model: Root cause: trg_Loyalty_sync updated Loyalty then Orders, while order placement updated Orders then Loyalty, producing a lock-order deadlock. Fix: aligned order (Orders → Loyalty) in the sync job, added 1205 retry. Verified: 0 deadlocks in 7 days in system_health.

lessons.title: Lab: Ticket — replica lag and oplog window

scenes.text: Alert: mongo03 is 45 minutes behind.
Find why, and check the oplog window before it goes stale.

steps.title: Key checks
steps.body: `rs.printSecondaryReplicationInfo()` for lag; `rs.printReplicationInfo()` for oplog window. If lag exceeds the window, the secondary becomes **stale** and needs a full resync.

steps.title: Common causes
steps.body: Slow disk on the secondary, network, heavy unindexed updates, a long index build.

steps.title: Mistake
steps.body: Reading from lagging secondaries with readPreference secondary for fresh data.

ticket.description: Alert: replication lag > 30 min on mongo03 (rs0). Started ~09:30 when the nightly price-update job was moved to daytime.

investigate.label: rs.printSecondaryReplicationInfo()
investigate.reveal: mongo02: 0 secs behind; mongo03: 2712 secs (45 min) behind the primary.

investigate.label: rs.printReplicationInfo() on primary
investigate.reveal: configured oplog size 2 GB; log length start to end: 1.4 hrs.

investigate.label: iostat on mongo03
investigate.reveal: Disk util 99%, await 85 ms — mongo03 is on an older HDD volume; mongo02 on SSD.

investigate.label: Application error rate
investigate.reveal: Normal; apps read from primary.

options: mongo03's slow HDD can't apply the heavy daytime update load; lag is approaching the 1.4 h oplog window
diagnosis.why: IO-bound secondary + bursty writes; risk of going stale if lag exceeds the window.

resolution: Throttle/batch the price-update job and move it off-peak
Increase the oplog size (replSetResizeOplog) to widen the window
Move mongo03 to SSD storage like the other members
Watch lag return to near 0
Add alert for lag > 50% of oplog window

closure.model: Root cause: daytime bulk price updates overwhelmed mongo03's HDD (99% util), lag reached 45 min vs a 1.4 h oplog window. Fix: throttled job and moved to 01:00, resized oplog to 10 GB, migrated mongo03 to SSD. Verified: lag < 2 s, oplog window 7 h.

steps.title: Data types
steps.body: Strings, hashes, lists, sets, sorted sets, streams; commands SET/GET with `EX` TTL, HSET/HGETALL, LPUSH/LRANGE, SADD, ZADD/ZRANGE, INCR (atomic counters), EXPIRE/TTL.

steps.title: Never KEYS * in production
steps.body: It blocks the single-threaded command loop; use SCAN with MATCH and COUNT.

steps.title: Mistakes

- Caching without TTLs
- Huge values (> 1 MB) and huge keys

steps.title: Memory controls
steps.body: `maxmemory` and `maxmemory-policy`: noeviction (default), allkeys-lru, allkeys-lfu, volatile-lru, volatile-ttl… For a pure cache use **allkeys-lru/lfu**. `INFO memory`, `MEMORY USAGE key`, `redis-cli --bigkeys`/`--memkeys`.

steps.body: `mem_fragmentation_ratio` well above ~1.5 may warrant `activedefrag yes`.

scenes.text: Spikes line up with Redis latency.
SLOWLOG and INFO reveal the culprit.

steps.title: Latency sources
steps.body: Single-threaded command execution: O(N) commands on big collections (HGETALL of a 2M-field hash, LRANGE 0 -1, SMEMBERS), KEYS, fork for RDB snapshots on large datasets with transparent huge pages, swapping.

steps.title: Tools
steps.body: `SLOWLOG GET 10`, `LATENCY DOCTOR`, `INFO persistence` (latest_fork_usec), `redis-cli --latency`.

steps.title: Fix in code
steps.body: Replace HGETALL on huge hashes with HSCAN or redesign the key.

ticket.short: Checkout p99 spikes to 2 s every ~10 min
ticket.description: Grafana shows checkout p99 spikes from 120 ms to ~2 s roughly every 10 minutes; Redis command latency spikes at the same time.

investigate.label: SLOWLOG GET 10
investigate.reveal: HGETALL promo:active (2,140,331 fields) taking 940 ms, called by the promo-refresh cron every 10 minutes.

investigate.label: INFO persistence
investigate.reveal: latest_fork_usec: 21000 — 21 ms, acceptable.

investigate.label: INFO memory
investigate.reveal: used_memory 9.2G of maxmemory 12G — fine.

investigate.label: Network to redis01
investigate.reveal: 0.3 ms RTT.

options: An O(N) HGETALL on a 2M-field hash blocking Redis every 10 minutes
diagnosis.why: The single-threaded event loop is blocked for ~1 s by HGETALL; all other commands queue.

resolution: Change promo-refresh to HSCAN in batches (or fetch only needed fields with HMGET)
Split promo:active into smaller per-category hashes
Deploy and confirm SLOWLOG no longer shows HGETALL
Watch checkout p99 for 24 h
Add an alert on SLOWLOG entries > 100 ms

closure.model: Root cause: promo-refresh cron ran HGETALL on promo:active (2.1M fields) every 10 min, blocking Redis ~940 ms and spiking checkout p99. Fix: HSCAN batches of 1,000 and split hash per category. Verified: no SLOWLOG entries > 10 ms; checkout p99 steady at 120 ms for 24 h.

outcomes: Learners can choose persistence
Learners can operate Sentinel failover
Learners can size Redis

scenes.text: A Redis restart lost 20 minutes of job-queue data.
Choose persistence that matches the data's value.

steps.title: Options
steps.body:
- **RDB** snapshots (`save 900 1` etc.): compact, fast restarts, can lose minutes
- **AOF** (`appendonly yes`) with `appendfsync everysec` (≤ ~1 s loss) or `always` (slow)
- Both together is common; AOF rewrite compacts the log

steps.title: Check
steps.body: `INFO persistence`: rdb_last_bgsave_status, aof_enabled, aof_last_write_status.

steps.title: Mistake
steps.body: A cache with AOF always on (needless latency) — or a queue with no persistence.

lessons.title: Lab: Mock interview — DBA technical round

story.title: Lab: Mock interview — DBA technical round

scenes.text: The DBA manager and a senior SRE interview you.
They want safe judgment under pressure.

steps.title: Format
steps.body: Technical questions across PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQL Server, MongoDB and Redis.

steps.title: Always mention
steps.body: Safety first (no data loss), measurement, rollback plan, communication.

steps.title: Red flags
steps.body: Deleting files to free space, skipping replication errors blindly, granting superuser casually.

rounds.q: A PostgreSQL query suddenly takes 30 s instead of 200 ms. Walk me through it.
rounds.model: Check pg_stat_activity for waits/locks, then EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) with real parameters. Compare estimated vs actual rows — stale stats or a plan flip are common, so ANALYZE the table. Check for missing/invalid indexes, bloat, or a blocking session. Fix, re-measure and monitor via pg_stat_statements.
followups: What if it only happens with some parameter values?

rounds.q: Explain RPO and RTO and how your backup design meets them.
rounds.model: RPO is maximum tolerable data loss; RTO is maximum time to restore. For RPO 15 min I'd archive WAL/take log backups at least every 15 minutes (or replicate); for RTO 1 h I'd keep recent full backups on fast storage and practise restores to prove the time. Test restores monthly.

rounds.q: How do you handle a deadlock reported by developers?
rounds.model: Get the deadlock details (PostgreSQL log, InnoDB status, SQL Server system_health), identify the two statements and resources, then fix access order or add indexes to reduce locked rows, keep transactions short, and make sure the app retries the victim.

rounds.q: Compare MongoDB replica sets and PostgreSQL streaming replication.
rounds.model: MongoDB replicates the oplog and has built-in elections with majority write concern. PostgreSQL ships WAL to standbys; automatic failover needs external tooling such as Patroni. Both need odd quorum members or witnesses to avoid split brain.

rounds.q: When would you choose Redis eviction allkeys-lru vs noeviction?
rounds.model: allkeys-lru for a pure cache where any key can be rebuilt; noeviction when Redis holds data you can't lose (queues, sessions), so writes fail loudly instead of silently dropping data.

tips: Close with how you would verify and monitor.

options: Grant a scoped, time-boxed, audited role

scenes.text: The DBA manager and a senior SRE interview you.
They want safe judgment under pressure.

steps.title: Format
steps.body: Pressure scenarios from real on-call shifts.

steps.title: Always mention
steps.body: Safety first (no data loss), measurement, rollback plan, communication.

steps.title: Red flags
steps.body: Deleting files to free space, skipping replication errors blindly, granting superuser casually.

rounds.q: At 2 AM the primary database disk is 98% full. What do you do?
rounds.model: Acknowledge the incident, check what grew (du), and look for the usual causes: WAL retained by an inactive replication slot or failing archive_command, runaway logs, or temp files. Free space safely (fix the archiver, drop the stale slot after confirming, rotate logs) or extend the volume. Never delete data or WAL files by hand. Then add alerts and capacity follow-ups.
followups: What if it's tempdb in SQL Server?

rounds.q: A developer asks for sysadmin/superuser to 'debug faster'.
rounds.model: I'd decline permanent superuser, understand what they need, and grant a specific role (read-only on prod, or elevated access in staging). If production access is truly needed, use time-boxed, approved, audited access.

rounds.q: Replication broke on a MySQL replica with a duplicate-key error. Do you skip it?
rounds.model: Not blindly. First find why the row exists (direct write, inconsistent seed), compare data, fix the conflicting row or re-seed, then enable super_read_only and run pt-table-checksum to verify no other drift.

tips: Close with how you would verify and monitor.

options: Grant a scoped, time-boxed, audited role

scenes.text: Orders (PostgreSQL) slow down while Redis cache hit rate drops.
Triage across systems.

steps.title: Approach
steps.body: Correlate timelines: cache misses → more DB load → slow queries. Fix the cause, not just symptoms.

steps.title: Look first
steps.body: Redis evictions/expired keys, DB active sessions and top queries.

steps.title: Comms
steps.body: Update the incident channel every 15 minutes.

ticket.short: Checkout slow; cache hit rate fell from 96% to 41%
ticket.description: Black Friday 19:05: checkout p99 6 s. Grafana: Redis hit rate dropped at 19:00; PostgreSQL active sessions 380 (normally 60).

investigate.label: Redis INFO stats
investigate.reveal: evicted_keys jumped from 0 to 1.8M since 19:00; used_memory at maxmemory 12 GB.

investigate.label: Recent changes
investigate.reveal: 19:00 marketing launched a 'recently viewed' feature caching full product JSON per user in the same Redis.

investigate.label: PostgreSQL pg_stat_statements
investigate.reveal: Product-by-id query calls ×9 vs normal — cache misses falling through.

investigate.label: PostgreSQL disk
investigate.reveal: Fine.

options: New per-user cache entries filled Redis, evicting product cache keys and flooding PostgreSQL
diagnosis.why: Eviction pressure from a new feature caused cache misses that overloaded the database.

resolution: Feature-flag off 'recently viewed' caching
Confirm Redis evictions stop and hit rate recovers > 90%
Confirm PostgreSQL active sessions and p99 return to normal
Move per-user data to a separate Redis with its own sizing/TTL
Post-incident review with capacity checks for new cache use

closure.model: Root cause: 'recently viewed' feature (19:00) stored large per-user JSON in the shared cache, hitting maxmemory and evicting 1.8M product keys; misses drove 9× product queries to PostgreSQL. Mitigation: flagged off at 19:18; hit rate 95% by 19:25, p99 180 ms. Prevention: separate Redis for user data, cache capacity review in launch checklist.
